title: 5 Questions To Mental Freedom
paragraphs: Many of the things I teach, you may sometimes not know why I teach them. But that's what motivates me. This is what motivates me. These are the five questions that make me wake up in the morning, talk to you, pray for you, teach, write books, sing, and write songs. The reason I hold conferences and what I strive for is these five questions. According to Jesus in the Gospel of Luke, chapter four, the anointing of God on him was to free the captives and set the oppressed free.

It is possible to be free and yet still be oppressed. What are the five questions? First, who am I? Most people have not yet answered this question. That is why they still dress like others, act like them, style their hair like them, and follow trends, moods, fashions, and what is popular. Why? They don't know who they are. They are trying to find themselves. Nothing is more damaging than trying to be someone you are not. Even the saints in the church still don't know who they are. They know where they are going.

They are going to heaven, but they do not know who they are. The second question we must answer is: Where am I from? Where am I from? If you don't know where you came from, you will remain in slavery. Now, many people believe they came from Africa, or England, or Poland, or China, or this place or that, and they keep returning to our physical heritage, so to speak. Look at this room. You are such a diverse mix that you don't know where you're going. Some of you have mixed white, black, and Indian ancestry.

Where would you go if you tried to go back in time to find yourself? You don't know where you're going. Therefore, we need to deal with something more important than just ethnic heritage. If you don't know where you came from, and you only use your race or ethnic origin, is that all? If you are only using this to try to find your heritage, you will run into trouble because you will find yourself torn between five or six different paths. The third question you must answer is: Why am I here?

A subjugated person lacks a sense of purpose. They don't know why they exist. This is the third question: Why am I here? The fourth question is, what can I do? We must answer this question in order to live effectively. What does this mean? What is my ability? What are my true potentials? What am I really capable of doing? If you are unable to answer the question of your ability and potential, people will dominate your powers. They will overpower you, control you, and literally tell you what you cannot do.

The fourth question is: " Where am I going?" Some people have no future. They have no direction. They have no sense of destiny. You need to know where you are going. When you are persecuted, these five questions are taken from you. When you are being persecuted, your persecutor answers these five questions. When you are persecuted, the persecutor determines who you are, where you come from, what you can do, why you are here, and where you are going. The oppressor dictates who you are.

Someone in South Africa told me that they had read that colored people were born only to fetch water and chop wood. So, this is what they taught the people in their church. In the church. Now, I have learned this over 300 years, and it will be difficult for you to change your attitude towards me. So, when I enter the room, even if I'm wearing a suit, she says, "That's a smart-looking lumberjack." Look, your mind hasn't changed. She says, " Well, this is a dignified water carrier." Why?

Because your mind hasn't changed mentally. There are people in our country who are still under the sway of the colonial mentality. There are people here who are still being persecuted. Even if they promote you, they don't accept you. Even if they allow you to wear a tie and be a supervisor, to them you are a supervisor for fetching water. She is still a woodcutter. Because the mindset needs renewal. God will bring about change when you change.

Now, the problem is that if the oppressed is liberated, the oppressor loses his power over him. I'll say this again. If the oppressed is freed, the oppressor loses his power over him. It is difficult for you to order me to do something or force me to do something when I know it is not my business. Therefore, we must understand that freedom is the key to living effectively, not salvation alone.
